briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Ballot Measures and Broken Contracts: Michigan Cannabis Braces for Hemp Crackdown as DEA Rescheduling Fight Resumes
briefs.top: Michigan voters in Mottville Township and Bad Axe will decide dueling dispensary bans in November, while a federal appeals court ruling that cannabis supply contracts can't be enforced in federal court sends a warning through the industry ahead of December's hemp crackdown. Nationally, the DEA and rescheduling opponents filed dueling briefs as the Schedule III fight resumes, Vireo Growth's pending deals would make it the country's largest cannabis retailer by store count, and a new study shows psilocybin easing chronic suicidal thoughts.

local.text: Mottville Township and Bad Axe put dispensaries to a vote — Mottville Township voters decide Nov. 3 whether to ban dispensaries outright, which would shutter the township's two existing pot shops, while Bad Axe voters weigh repealing their city's ordinance banning marijuana retailers.

Appeals court rules cannabis supply contracts unenforceable in federal court — The 6th Circuit wiped out a roughly $32 million jury verdict Hello Farms had won against Curaleaf subsidiaries, holding that federal courts can't enforce agreements built around a federally illegal drug, a precedent now binding in Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, and Tennessee.

Federal hemp crackdown looms as untested gas-station THC stays legal until December — New federal rules targeting intoxicating hemp products take effect in December, and Michigan retailers have already begun pulling items from shelves ahead of a deadline regulators hope closes the loophole letting unlicensed shops sell untested hemp.

Caregivers-turned-retailer Zasso sells ounces for about $100 — The five-person Michigan outfit, started by former medical caregivers, is one of the small operators surviving the state's price collapse by keeping overhead low and selling direct.

Michigan Supreme Court orders expedited review of 24% wholesale tax challenge — The court sent the cannabis industry's lawsuit over the wholesale tax back to the Court of Appeals with instructions to expedite its review, leaving the tax in place while the fight over its constitutionality continues.

national.text: DEA and rescheduling opponents file dueling briefs ahead of key hearing — Both sides submitted new filings in the marijuana rescheduling proceeding, keeping the Schedule III push alive even as the broader process stays paused pending review of a new GAO report.

FDA seeks industry input on ibogaine clinical trial design — The agency issued a request for information on how an early-stage ibogaine study should be structured, a step that could speed the psychedelic's path toward approved treatment despite its known cardiac risks.

New study: psilocybin eases chronic suicidal thoughts — Researchers found 70% of participants with longstanding suicidal ideation reported little or none by week 12 after psilocybin-assisted therapy, outlasting the shorter-term relief typically seen with ketamine.

Vireo Growth's pending deals would make it the largest U.S. cannabis retailer — Assuming its FLUENT and C21 acquisitions close, Vireo says it will operate roughly 270 dispensaries nationwide, after posting Q2 revenue of $209.3 million, up 335% year-over-year.

Cronos Group pushes CanAdelaar acquisition deadline to Oct. 15 — The cannabis company extended the long-stop date on its pending deal by another month as the transaction works through remaining regulatory approvals.
